name: Lyo.FileSystemWatcher
tagline: Snapshot-based file watcher for .NET. Detects creates, deletes, changes, moves, and renames with debounce and SHA256 hashing.
description: Snapshot-based file watcher for .NET. Detects creates, deletes, changes, moves, and renames with debounce and SHA256 hashing.
features: **Snapshot-based change detection.** Compares directory snapshots instead of relying only on FileSystemWatcher events.
**Debouncing.** Batches rapid changes so you do not get an event storm.
**Hash-based move detection.** Detects file moves and renames even when the file system does not report them.
**File and directory events.** Separate events with `FileSystemChangeInfo` payloads.
**Thread-safe.** Safe to use from multiple threads.
**Options.** `FileSystemWatcherOptions` for debounce, hashing, path comparison, and subdirectory watching.
**Errors.** Snapshot and detection failures go to `Error` and to `ILogger` when you pass one.

sections.title: File events
items: `FileCreated`. Fired when a file is created.
`FileDeleted`. Fired when a file is deleted.
`FileChanged`. Fired when a file's content is modified.
`FileMoved`. Fired when a file is moved to a different directory.
`FileRenamed`. Fired when a file is renamed (moved within same directory).

sections.title: Directory events
items: `DirectoryCreated`. Fired when a directory is created.
`DirectoryDeleted`. Fired when a directory is deleted.
`DirectoryChanged`. Fired when a directory's content changes.
`DirectoryMoved`. Fired when a directory is moved to a different parent.
`DirectoryRenamed`. Fired when a directory is renamed (moved within same parent).

sections.title: General events
items: `OnAnyChange`. Fired for any file or directory change.
`Error`. Fired when snapshot or change detection fails.

sections.title: Event data
sections.body:
All events provide a `FileSystemChangeInfo` object with the following properties:

```csharp
public sealed record FileSystemChangeInfo(
    string? OldPath, // Previous path (null for created items)
    string? NewPath, // New path (null for deleted items)
    ChangeTypeEnum ChangeType, // Type of change
    bool IsDirectory, // True if directory, false if file
    int? OldFileCount = null, // Directory: files before change
    int? OldDirectoryCount = null,// Directory: subdirectories before change
    int? NewFileCount = null, // Directory: files after change
    int? NewDirCount = null) // Directory: subdirectories after change
```

sections.title: Metrics integration
sections.text: When `EnableMetrics` is set to `true` and an `IMetrics` instance is provided, the following metrics are recorded:

sections.title: Snapshot metrics
items: `filesystemwatcher.snapshot.duration`. Duration of snapshot operations (timing).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.duration_ms`. Duration of snapshot operations in milliseconds (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.file_count`. Number of files in snapshot (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.directory_count`. Number of directories in snapshot (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.item_count`. Total items in snapshot (gauge).

sections.title: Change detection metrics
items: `filesystemwatcher.change_detection.duration`. Duration of change detection (timing).
`filesystemwatcher.change_detection.duration_ms`. Duration of change detection in milliseconds (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.changes.detected`. Number of changes detected per scan (gauge).

sections.title: Error handling
File hashing
items: **Enabled (default).** Accurate move/rename detection. Slower on large directories.
**Disabled.** Faster. Move detection relies on file system events only.

sections.title: Memory usage
items: Snapshots store the complete directory tree in memory
For very large directory structures (10,000+ files), consider:
Disabling file hashing
Increasing debounce delay
Monitoring memory usage

sections.title: Debounce delay
items: **Lower values (50-100ms).** Faster response, higher CPU usage.
**Higher values (500-1000ms).** Slower response, lower CPU usage.
**Default (250ms).** A reasonable default for most directories.

sections.title: Expected snapshot times
items: **Small directories (< 100 files).** Under 100ms per snapshot.
**Medium directories (100-1000 files).** 100-500ms per snapshot.
**Large directories (> 1000 files).** 500ms+ per snapshot. Hashing large files stretches this.

sections.title: Thread safety
Disposal
Troubleshooting: events not firing
items: **Check path exists.** The directory must exist when creating the watcher.
**Check permissions.** You need read access to the directory.
**Check debounce delay.** Very rapid changes may be batched together.
**Check event handlers.** Subscribe before changes occur.
**Wait for initial snapshot.** The watcher needs time to take the first snapshot.

sections.title: Troubleshooting: high CPU usage
items: **Disable file hashing.** Set `EnableFileHashing = false`.
**Increase debounce delay.** Higher values reduce CPU usage.
**Watch snapshot frequency.** Too many rapid changes can spike CPU.

sections.title: Troubleshooting: memory usage
items: **Watch snapshot size.** Large directory trees consume more memory.
**Disable hashing.** Reduces memory per file entry.
**Dispose the watcher.** Leaks show up if you leave it running.

sections.title: Troubleshooting: missing move/rename events
items: **Enable file hashing.** Required for reliable move/rename detection.
**Check the file system.** Some file systems do not report move events.
**Check timing.** Very rapid moves may show up as delete+create.
**Directory moves.** The directory name must stay the same (different parent, same name).

sections.title: Known limitation: file move bug
sections.text: There is a known bug where directory change events for the source directory when moving a file show incorrect counts. The destination directory works correctly.

sections.title: Known limitations: performance
items: File hashing can be slow on large files or many files
Snapshot operations are synchronous and can block briefly
Very large directory structures consume significant memory

sections.title: Known limitations: directory move detection
items: Directory move detection only works when the directory name stays the same but the parent changes
If both name and parent change, it will be detected as delete + create

sections.title: Architecture: snapshot-based detection
sections.text: The watcher takes periodic snapshots of the directory tree and diffs them. That is more reliable than FileSystemWatcher events alone.

sections.title: Architecture: debouncing
sections.text: Multiple rapid changes are batched together using a debounce timer to prevent event storms and reduce CPU usage.

sections.title: Architecture: hash-based move detection
sections.text: File hashing (SHA256) is used to detect moves and renames even when the file system doesn't provide this information directly.

sections.title: Architecture: error resilience
items: Event handler exceptions are caught and logged, preventing one faulty handler from crashing the watcher
Snapshot errors are caught and reported via the Error event
Cancellation tokens allow graceful shutdown of long-running operations

rows: Snapshot-based, debounced watcher (`IDisposable`). Constructor: `FileSystemWatcher(string path, FileSystemWatcherOptions?, ILogger?, IMetrics?)`. Raises the file/directory/`OnAnyChange`/`Error` events listed above.
`record` payload emitted by every change event.
In-memory snapshot of the watched tree used for diffing.
Metric and tag name constants (see snapshot, change detection, event, and error metrics above).
